independent_theorem_review.bounded_trim_hull: A nonempty bounded coherent affine trimmed face lies in the convex hull of its complete boundary. Every finite line boundary segment lies in the convex hull of its two endpoints. Applying the same injective affine surface map preserves convex hull inclusion. This is conditional on exact bounded trim/material coherence, which is not supplied by native validity alone.
independent_theorem_review.whole_bounded_material: Every compact material lies in the convex hull of its boundary. An invertible oblique-coordinate box containing every complete coherent boundary generator therefore contains that material; its continuous translation segment is covered by including both endpoint generators.
independent_theorem_review.added_boundary: For a closed bounded material S and a convex displacement set D containing zero, every x in (S+D) outside S has a last crossing of boundary(S) along its defining segment. Its remaining displacement lies in D. Thus S+D is contained in S union (boundary(S)+D). Summing nonnegative carrier volumes gives an upper bound, provided S and its complete boundary have the stated exact semantics.
independent_theorem_review.terminal_affine_source: For the strict degree-one, two-pole, two-knot, [2,2], nonperiodic nonrational subclass, the independently read source path leaves the actual parameter unchanged and performs a single affine blend. Every scalar affine extremum on a finite interval occurs at an endpoint, including the 12 actual terminal overshoots.
independent_theorem_review.support_basis: Choosing a nonsingular support coordinate basis from each original q-law changes the enclosing set calculation, not the original displacement or any original acceptance threshold.
